provenance: Telephone call, 2026-09-03. Larry's son asked the tier-1 questions from the interview guide and reported this answer in his own words; third-person voice, so it is a paraphrase. Raw capture: research/interviews/breakfast-questions.md.
text: He says Camp Zama may have been 9/3/1965. He said he was kind of in and out of it. He remembers being conscious in Subic Bay and in a room with some Russian Archaoligist who had gotten sick somewhere in the Northern part of cambodia and they had gotten out of there and into Subic Bay Naval Hospital. We played cards together.
researchNotes: THE ANSWER TO THE ARCHIVE'S MOST-WANTED FACT, and it validates a derivation made the previous day. Working the medevac chain backwards from "early September" had put his last day on the mountain at about 25-27 August 1965; an arrival of 3 September 1965 puts it at about 25-26 August. The derivation and his memory agree. Filed as paraphrase because the block is third-person reporting, although its final sentence ("We played cards together") is Larry's own voice - the son's summary and Larry's words are interleaved here and the record should not be read as a verbatim transcript. Held loosely for two reasons: he offers the date as "may have been", and he says he was "kind of in and out of it", which is exactly the condition under which dates blur. The Russian archaeologist at Subic Bay Naval Hospital, invalided out of northern Cambodia, is new to the archive and is the kind of specific, checkable detail that tends to be true.
